Summary Description: Dr. Miroslav Kramár specializes in the interface between mathematics and physics, with a focus on computational topology, persistent homology, and dynamical systems applied to granular matter and complex networks. His work advances topological methods to analyze force networks, stick-slip phenomena, and global dynamical structure, while integrating data-driven approaches (e.g., MLCD) to discretize phase space and compute Conley indices. This combination enables robust, scalable analyses that extract meaningful global insights from high-dimensional, noisy data and experimental measurements, with demonstrated applicability across disk and polygon granular systems and beyond.

Representative Publications.Title: On intermittency in sheared granular systems
Representative Publications.Context: Introduces local/mesoscale PH-based measures and differential force networks to signal impending slips in 2D granular systems; contrasts global vs local indicators for slip forecasting.

Representative Publications.Title: Machine learning approach to force reconstruction in photoelastic materials
Representative Publications.Context: Combines CNN-based force reconstruction with transfer learning to infer inter-particle forces from photoelastic patterns; demonstrates cross-size transferability and efficiency improvements over traditional methods.

Representative Publications.Title: Evolution of force networks during stick-slip motion of an intruder in a granular material: Topological measures extracted from experimental data
Representative Publications.Context: Applies persistent homology to experimental force networks (disks and pentagons) to identify slip precursors and characterize topology-driven evolution during stick-slip cycles.

Representative Publications.Title: Intruder in a two-dimensional granular system: statics and dynamics of force networks in an experimental system experiencing stick-slip dynamics
Representative Publications.Context: Examines G2-derived force networks and PH-based metrics to reveal stick-slip precursors and network evolution, highlighting differences between disk and pentagon packings.

Representative Publications.Title: Machine-Learned Cubical Decomposition (MLCD) for Conley indices
Representative Publications.Context: Introduces a data-driven cubical decomposition approach to approximate attractors and Conley indices with substantially fewer cells than regular grids, enabling higher-dimensional analysis and providing a scalable pipeline for dynamical systems in data.
